verdict.rationale: Grafana's own docs describe running parts of the stack locally: Loki in single-binary mode on a local filesystem, fed by Grafana Alloy, and Mimir in monolithic mode with no added dependencies. File-based provisioning lets developers define dashboards and data sources in version-controlled files, and the CLI is described as suitable for local development. Community users also report self-hosting Grafana with InfluxDB and Telegraf. missing for 10: an explicit first-party quickstart for running the Grafana server itself locally (e.g. a Docker or binary install guide), a documented end-to-end local stack (e.g. docker-compose) for instrumentation testing, and independent hands-on confirmation of the local dev workflow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can spin up a local or dev instance of the platform to test instrumentation and dashboards

citations.quote: Try it locally. The fastest way to experiment is to run Loki in monolithic (single-binary) mode with a local filesystem backend and send logs to it with Grafana Alloy.
Use the monolithic mode to get up and running with just one binary and no added dependencies.
You can define data sources and dashboards using files that can be version controlled, making GitOps more natural.
It’s suitable for CI/CD pipelines, local development
